expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: | { id: SubscriptionId; status: "trialing"; trialEndDate: Date } | { id: SubscriptionId; status: "active"; renewalDate: Date } | ... — status is the discriminant

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: trialing variant only has trialEndDate, active only renewalDate, past_due only retryCount and gracePeriodEndDate, canceled only cancellation info

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: assertNever function provided; used in renewalCopy switch with default: return assertNever(sub)

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: SubscriptionId branded using Brand<string, "SubscriptionId"> pattern with unique symbol

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: transition function is provided only as a stub throwing 'not implemented'; no actual constraint on state changes

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Misuse check section lists: reading .trialEndDate off active sub, missing new status in switch, mixing reason/voluntary contradiction

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary recommendation is discriminated union; explicitly contrasts with optional-fields design in Insight section
